evals.name: babysit-loop-config-resolution-and-merge-floor
evals.prompt:
/source-control:babysit-loop melodic-software/example-repo autopilot --merge full-autonomy

Headless launch under /loop. The team-tracked .claude/source-control.md sets babysit_loop_merge to c2-mechanical and babysit_loop_stop_mode to standing; no user-global or local overlay exists; no other loop keys are set.
evals.expected_output: The lane accepts the required owner/repo argument and resolves config as arguments over the layered seam over tier defaults, reporting which source supplied each value. This line does NOT widen the merge dimension, and the lane says exactly why. The literal autopilot tier keyword widens dimensions 1-5 and 7 but is merge-inert by itself: the convention's one named exception fires only when the invocation's own argument line types both the autopilot tier keyword and the dedicated raise argument --merge c3-this-run, and this line's merge argument is full-autonomy instead. Every merge-dimension value other than c3-this-run may only select a lower rung, so --merge full-autonomy is ignored and reported — standing merge-rung raises bind from the team-tracked layer only, and nothing on this line reaches full-autonomy. The effective merge rung is therefore the tracked c2-mechanical. Had the line typed --merge c3-this-run alongside autopilot, the widening would cover this single invocation up to C3, persisting nothing, never reaching C4-structural or C5-untrusted-provenance, which stay human-merge under every rung, seam value, and argument, and applying only because the team-tracked file carrying loop-lane keys is the recorded lane adoption — with no tracked loop-lane keys at all the merge dimension resolves human-only and the exception does not apply either. Eligibility stays a work-class test irrespective of author, with bot authorship alone never qualifying and an unlinked or unclassified PR never eligible at any rung. An argument selecting a lower rung (for example --merge human-only) would have been honored. Being headless, the lane never blocks on an interview: it takes the resolved config and logs the assumption per the convention's headless-config floor. Each cycle invokes /source-control:babysit-prs with the resolved tier and repo scope rather than restating its tier matrix, wrappers, or safety discipline.
expectations: Requires the owner/repo argument and refuses to guess a repository when it is absent
Resolves invocation args over the layered babysit_loop_* seam keys over tier defaults, and reports which source supplied each effective value

Keeps the merge dimension at the tracked c2-mechanical: the typed autopilot tier keyword is merge-inert by itself, the exception requires the paired --merge c3-this-run raise argument on the same line, and the --merge full-autonomy argument is ignored and reported because every other merge value only ever lowers and standing raises bind from the team-tracked layer only

States that the paired widening, when typed, persists nothing — the next invocation omitting either token reverts to the tracked c2-mechanical rung — and that a lower-rung argument would have been honored
Holds the C4/C5 floor: no rung, seam value, or invocation argument, including this widening and including full-autonomy, ever grants merge authority over a structural or untrusted-provenance item

Treats the team-tracked loop-lane keys as the recorded lane adoption that activates the c2-mechanical baseline — absent any tracked adoption the merge dimension resolves human-only and the explicit-autopilot exception does not apply either
States eligibility as a work-class test irrespective of author — bot authorship alone never qualifying, and an unlinked or unclassified PR never eligible at any rung
Never blocks headless on a mini-interview; logs the assumption per the headless-config floor
Invokes /source-control:babysit-prs per cycle with the resolved tier and scope instead of restating its tier matrix, guarded wrappers, or safety discipline
Names capability tiers only (frontier/strong/fast) and never a hard-coded model ID

evals.name: babysit-loop-grace-window-guard-floor-and-do-not-merge
evals.prompt:
/source-control:babysit-loop melodic-software/example-repo worker

Mid-cycle state: PR #41's head moved 10 minutes ago; PR #42 received a new review comment 20 minutes ago; PR #43 is a zero-blocker draft carrying a do-not-merge label; PR #44 is quiet, green, and gate-provable, and its work item classifies C2 mechanical. The tee file at ~/.claude/rate-limit-guard/rate-limits.json shows five_hour used_percentage 93 with a fresh captured_at. babysit_loop_grace_window_minutes is unset.
evals.expected_output: At cycle start the lane re-reads its durable state block, classifies guard mode, and takes the cycle-start snapshot. PRs #41 and #42 fall inside the default 30-minute activity grace window, and #43 carries WIP signals (draft + do-not-merge), so all three are report-only this cycle: never elevated, never thread-resolved, never merged; the do-not-merge label is respected and never stripped absent the explicit --strip-do-not-merge flag. PR #44 is the only PR the deterministic rung partition marks merge-eligible — its close-linked work item's recorded classification is C2 mechanical — so the worker-tier invocation is scoped to that single PR ref (/source-control:babysit-prs worker owner/repo#44), whose own expected-head pins, HEAD assertion, and deterministic merge gate still govern; the other PRs are never presented to a merge-capable invocation, and a PR with no close-linked item or no recorded classification would fail closed to the non-merge pass. On the 93% reading the lane drains in-flight work, stops starting new work, pauses until the tripped window's resets_at, arms a session Monitor on the tee file while paused, latches rate_limit_latch in durable state, and records guard mode in telemetry. The telemetry upsert is fail-closed: a failed comment lookup skips the upsert for the cycle rather than posting a duplicate comment.
expectations: Re-reads the machine-readable durable loop state from the telemetry comment at cycle start rather than trusting conversation context
Marks the head-moved and recently-commented PRs report-only under the default 30-minute grace window — no elevation, thread resolution, or merge
Never elevates the draft carrying WIP signals, and never removes a do-not-merge label without the explicit --strip-do-not-merge flag

Computes merge eligibility mechanically before invoking babysit-prs — close-linked work item resolved via the provider's close-linkage, classification read from the triage stamp — and scopes the merge-capable invocation to eligible PR refs only, failing closed on unlinked or unclassified PRs
Lets the quiet C2-mechanical PR proceed through the per-PR worker pass, deferring head pinning and the merge gate to that skill by citation
On the 93% tee reading: drains in-flight work, stops claiming, pauses until the tripped window's resets_at, and arms a session Monitor on the tee file while paused
Latches rate_limit_latch in durable state and records guard mode in the telemetry block
Treats a failed telemetry comment lookup as skip-this-cycle (fail closed), never as license to post a second comment
Parses tee-file session fields only with a JSON parser and never string-interpolates them into a shell command or prompt

evals.name: babysit-loop-drain-exit-terminal-state-and-pacing
evals.prompt:
/source-control:babysit-loop melodic-software/example-repo worker --drain

Cycle end. The cycle-start snapshot shows 0 open PRs and three open issues: 'Lane telemetry: babysit-loop', 'Lane telemetry: work-loop', and one issue carrying the human-gated role label with a machine-marked escalation comment and no PR in flight. Durable state shows cycle=17, backoff_level=3.
evals.expected_output: The drain evaluation runs against the cycle-start snapshot. Both telemetry tracking issues match the Lane telemetry: <lane> title contract and are excluded from the 0-open-issues evaluation as lane infrastructure. The one remaining open issue is human-gated/escalated with no PR in flight, which is the drain-terminal state per the loop-lane convention: the lane writes its final report, updates the durable state block on the telemetry comment, and stops cleanly instead of idling forever or chasing the escalation. Escalation state is read from the role label resolved via the consumer's .work-item-tracker.json config.role_labels (never a literal comparison) plus the machine-marked comment. Had the loop continued, the next cycle would be scheduled with ScheduleWakeup inside the [60, 3600] second clamp, mapped from the engine's recommended_cadence per the babysit-prs loop reference; a cycle-budget or seven-day-expiry hit would write a restart-request into the state block and stop cleanly rather than attempting a self-relaunch.
expectations: Evaluates the drain exit against the cycle-start snapshot, reporting rather than chasing mid-cycle intake
Excludes both Lane telemetry: <lane> issues from the 0-open-issues evaluation as lane infrastructure, and never works, closes, or waits on them
Recognizes the drain-terminal state — every remaining open item human-gated or escalated and no PR in flight — and stops cleanly with a final report
Resolves the human-gated role label through the consumer's config.role_labels map, never a literal label comparison
Updates the durable state block (cycle count, backoff level, no-progress streak) in the telemetry comment before stopping
When continuing, schedules via ScheduleWakeup within the [60, 3600] clamp using the cadence mapping owned by the babysit-prs loop reference
On a cycle-budget or seven-day-expiry hit, writes a restart-request into the telemetry state block and stops cleanly rather than relaunching itself

evals.name: babysit-loop-autopilot-exception-is-typed-only-never-inherited
evals.prompt:
/source-control:babysit-loop melodic-software/example-repo

Headless launch under /loop, no tier keyword on the invocation line. The team-tracked .claude/source-control.md sets babysit_loop_tier to autopilot and babysit_loop_merge to c2-mechanical. The user's plugin userConfig sets babysit_default_tier to autopilot. This cycle's snapshot has PR #7 (item classifies C3, green, one unresolved review thread), PR #8 (item classifies C4 structural, green, no blockers), and PR #9 (green, no blockers, opened from a fork in an outside account — the head repository differs from the base — closing an internally triaged C2-mechanical issue).
evals.expected_output: The lane resolves the autopilot tier from the team-tracked babysit_loop_tier and runs dimensions 1-5 and 7 at that tier. It does NOT apply the merge-rung exception: the exception fires only when the invocation's own argument line types both the literal autopilot tier keyword and the dedicated raise argument --merge c3-this-run, and here neither token was typed — the tier was inherited from a config layer, and both tokens are never inherited, never defaulted, never supplied by a config layer. babysit_default_tier is a babysit-prs key for a bare invocation of that skill and never supplies this lane's tier at all, let alone the exception. So the effective merge rung is the tracked c2-mechanical: PR #7 classifies C3, is outside the rung, and routes to the safe per-PR pass with its unresolved thread escalating rather than drawing a pre-escalation resolver dispatch. PR #8 classifies C4 and is excluded before the rung comparison even runs — the C4/C5 floor is unconditional and no tier keyword, config value, or argument reaches it. PR #9 is excluded too, and for a different reason: C5 is a provenance test on the PR itself, so a cross-repository fork PR is C5 whatever its close-linked item's recorded class says — the class travels with the code's provenance, not with the issue it closes. The lane reports the tier source and the merge-rung source separately so the distinction is visible rather than inferred.
expectations: Applies the config-supplied autopilot tier to dimensions 1-5 and 7 but NOT to the merge dimension — the exception requires both the literal autopilot tier keyword and the dedicated --merge c3-this-run raise argument typed on this invocation's own line, never inherited, defaulted, or supplied by a config layer
Treats babysit_default_tier as a babysit-prs key for a bare invocation of that skill, never a source of this lane's tier and never a route to the exception
Keeps the effective merge rung at the tracked c2-mechanical, so the C3 PR is outside the rung and routes to the safe per-PR pass
Escalates the C3 PR's unresolved thread normally — the fresh-subagent pre-escalation resolver is reachable only under the typed autopilot + --merge c3-this-run exception
Excludes the C4 structural PR before the rung comparison, unconditionally, citing the autonomy matrix's never-promotes contract rather than a rung value

Excludes the fork PR as C5 on the PR's own cross-repository provenance rather than the C2 class recorded on the item it closes, and does not reach that verdict by comparing an author login to the watched-owner allowlist
Reports the tier source and the merge-rung source separately rather than collapsing them into one effective tier

evals.name: babysit-loop-no-progress-detector-idle-vs-stalled
evals.prompt:
/source-control:babysit-loop melodic-software/example-repo worker

Cycle end. Durable state: no_progress_streak=2. The cycle-start snapshot held two open PRs, both WIP drafts with non-green checks; since the previous cycle no PR merged or closed, no head moved, no review or comment activity, no checks transition, no draft elevated, and the lane wrote no new escalation. babysit_loop_no_progress_threshold is unset. No open issue titled 'Lane stall: babysit-loop' exists.
evals.expected_output: Open PRs in the cycle-start snapshot are actionable work in view even when the grace-window overlay marks them report-only, and nothing qualifying happened since the previous cycle — no merge or close, no material change by anyone, no new escalation — so the no-progress streak increments to 3, reaching the unset seam key's default threshold of 3. The lane raises the stall escalation through the existing escalation contract: an issue titled exactly 'Lane stall: babysit-loop' carrying the human-gated role label (resolved from the consumer's config.role_labels, canonical needs-human default with a loud notice when the binding file is absent) plus a machine-marked comment whose first line is the work-items escalation marker with lane=babysit-loop kind=escalated, reporting the streak length, the cycles covered, and what sat unmoved. Before creating it the lane checks for an existing open stall issue matched on the exact title AND its own write identity as author — at most one open; a third party's lookalike never suppresses the signal. The stall escalation itself never counts as qualifying progress, and a lane-authored fix re-attempting the same still-unresolved blocker on a later cycle never re-qualifies either — the detector measures the queue moving, not the lane retrying. The lane escalates and keeps looping — never stops on a stall. A cycle whose snapshot held zero open PRs would be idle and hold the counter unchanged; foreign activity — a head move, a review comment, a checks transition — is the queue moving and resets the counter to zero, and when progress resumes while the stall issue is still open the lane records the resumption as a comment on it and leaves the disposition to the operator. The updated no_progress_streak persists in the telemetry state block, and the stall issue is ordinary human-gated backlog to the drain evaluation, never lane infrastructure.
expectations: Treats open PRs in the cycle-start snapshot as actionable work in view even when the grace-window overlay marks them report-only, and increments the streak because nothing qualifying happened since the previous cycle
Reads the threshold from the babysit_loop_no_progress_threshold seam key and applies the default of 3 when it is unset

Raises the stall escalation through the existing escalation contract: a 'Lane stall: babysit-loop' issue with the human-gated role label resolved from config.role_labels plus the machine-marked lane=babysit-loop kind=escalated comment
Checks for an existing open stall issue matched on exact title AND its own write identity as author before creating one — at most one open, and a third-party lookalike never suppresses the signal
Never counts the stall escalation itself as qualifying progress, and never lets a lane-authored repeat attempt at the same still-unresolved blocker re-qualify — only its first landing counts
Keeps looping after escalating — never stops the lane on a stall — and persists the updated no_progress_streak in the telemetry state block

Holds the counter on an idle cycle (zero open PRs in the snapshot) and on a guard-held one (rate_limit_latch set, so the lane starts no new mutating work — held even after the pause end, until a fresh healthy snapshot clears the latch), and resets it to zero on qualifying progress, foreign activity included — a head move, review or comment activity, or a checks transition is the queue moving — recording a resumption comment on the still-open stall issue when progress returns and leaving the disposition to the operator
Treats the stall issue as ordinary human-gated backlog for the drain evaluation, never as excluded lane infrastructure
